title: Maximum Product of Two Digits
statement: Take the decimal digits of the positive integer `n`, choose two of them sitting at two different positions, and multiply them. Return the largest product that such a choice can give. A digit value may be used twice only when it occurs at least twice in `n`.
notes:
## Intuition

Digits are never negative, so a product of two digits grows when either factor grows. The best pair is therefore the two largest digits of `n`, counting a repeated digit twice. Trying every pair of positions also works, but a single pass that remembers the top two digits is enough.

## Approach

1. Start `first` (largest digit so far) and `second` (second largest) at 0.
2. Peel off the last digit with `n % 10`.
3. If `digit` beats `first`, the old `first` moves down to `second` and `digit` takes its place.
4. Otherwise, if `digit` beats `second`, it replaces `second`.
5. Drop the last digit with `Math.floor(n / 10)` and repeat until `n` is 0, then return `first * second`.

## Example 1, step by step

`n = 31`. The first `digit` is 1, which beats `first = 0`, so `second = 0` and `first = 1`; `n` becomes 3. The next `digit` is 3, which beats `first`, so `second = 1` and `first = 3`; `n` becomes 0. The answer is `3 * 1 = 3`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(log n): one step per decimal digit, at most 10 here.
- Space: O(1): only two remembered digits.

## Pitfalls

- A repeated digit must be allowed to fill both places: `22` gives 4. Collecting the digits in a set loses the copy.
- When a new largest digit arrives, shift the old `first` into `second` instead of discarding it.
- Zeros count as digits: `10` gives `1 * 0 = 0`. Starting both places at 0 is safe because `n` has at least two digits.
- In JavaScript, `n / 10` is a fraction; use `Math.floor` to drop a digit.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `n` | the remaining number; its last digit is read next |
| `digit` | the digit just peeled off |
| `first` | largest digit seen so far |
| `second` | second largest digit seen so far, from a different position |

narration.2: first holds the largest digit seen so far; 0 is a safe start because n has at least two digits.
narration.3: second holds the second largest digit, taken from a different position.
narration.4: Keep going while n still has digits left.
narration.5: Peel off the last digit of n.
narration.6: Is this digit larger than the largest one so far?
narration.7: Yes: the old largest digit moves down to second place...
narration.9: Otherwise it may still beat the second largest, which also covers a repeat of the largest digit.
narration.10: Remember it as the second largest.
narration.12: Drop the last digit; Math.floor keeps n a whole number.
narration.14: The two largest digits give the largest product.
